steps.name: QC and gene filtering for 2x2 design
caveats: 12000 x 17 counts.csv has one gene-symbol column plus 16 sample columns; verify column count matches the 16 metadata rows before filtering
steps.question: Are the 16 samples in counts.csv (12000 genes) correctly balanced 4x across the WT/KO x vehicle/drug cells per metadata.csv, and which genes pass an expression filter for modeling?
constraints: Use the actual genotype (WT, KO) and treatment (vehicle, drug) labels from metadata.csv, not generic condition names
Do not drop samples without confirming the 4-replicate-per-cell design first
acceptance_criteria: Confirms 4 replicates in each of the 4 genotype x treatment cells and that count matrix sample columns match metadata rows
Produces a filtered count matrix removing low-count genes (e.g., filterByExpr or CPM-based rule)
Produces PCA/MDS on variance-stabilized filtered counts colored by genotype and treatment plus a sample-correlation heatmap
Filtered matrix and cleaned metadata are saved for the DESeq2 step

steps.name: DESeq2 factorial model: interaction term and simple effects
caveats: With n=4 per cell, power to detect a genotype x treatment interaction is modest; report this explicitly rather than treating a non-significant interaction as evidence of 'no difference'
A significant simple effect in only one genotype does not by itself establish a significant interaction — only the interaction term does
steps.question: Does the vehicle-vs-drug effect differ between WT and KO (genotype:treatment interaction), and how does the drug effect look separately within WT and within KO?
constraints: Reference levels must be WT for genotype and vehicle for treatment so the interaction coefficient represents the extra drug effect in KO relative to WT
Do not conflate the LRT interaction p-value with the simple-effect p-values in the summary — they answer different questions
acceptance_criteria: Fits DESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment on the filtered counts from T1S1
Reports the interaction term via likelihood-ratio test (full vs. reduced model without interaction) with log2FC, LRT statistic, p-value and BH-FDR
Reports apeglm/ashr-shrunken log2FCs for the interaction term and for both simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO)
Reports overlap and concordance/discordance in direction between the two simple-effect gene lists and the interaction-significant gene list
Produces dispersion plot, PCA of VST data by genotype/treatment, MA and volcano plots for the interaction and each simple effect, and a heatmap of top interaction genes across all 16 samples

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of genotype-dependent drug response
caveats: GO-BP is a nested hierarchy; expect correlated blocks of significant terms rather than independent hits
WikiPathways set names must be recovered by splitting the '%'-delimited descriptor field before reporting readable pathway names
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched specifically in the genotype:treatment interaction gene set versus enriched similarly in both the WT and KO drug-vs-vehicle simple effects?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 -> fgsea/clusterProfiler enrichment workflow (Love et al. 2014, PMID 25516281) for a factorial interaction contrast; no disputed rule applies.

constraints: Use only the human-symbol gene set collections (Hallmark, GO-BP, WikiPathways) since the counts data is Homo sapiens gene symbols — do not use the mouse or rat GMTs
acceptance_criteria: Runs fgsea preranked enrichment on the interaction-term statistic and on each simple-effect statistic (WT drug-vs-vehicle, KO drug-vs-vehicle) against human Hallmark, human GO Biological Process, and human WikiPathways gene sets
Runs overrepresentation analysis on the interaction-significant gene subset (FDR<0.05) against the same three human collections
Distinguishes and reports pathways unique to the interaction term (genotype-dependent drug response) from pathways shared by both simple effects (genotype-independent drug response)
Collapses GO parent/child redundancy before reporting a pathway hit count

steps.name: Network and TF-activity context for interaction genes
caveats: STRING and DoRothEA edges/targets are computational predictions, not confirmed mechanisms — report hub/TF findings as hypotheses, not established regulatory links
The full STRING graph (6.9M edges) is too dense for meaningful distance measures; restrict to combined_score>=700 before any topology analysis
steps.question: Which hub genes (via human PPI) and transcription factors (via human regulons) are implicated by the genes whose drug response differs between WT and KO?
constraints: protein.links.v12.0.txt.gz is space-delimited despite the .txt extension and must be parsed accordingly
Each STRING edge appears twice (once per direction) — deduplicate before reporting an edge count
acceptance_criteria: Joins the human STRING protein.info and protein.links files to map interaction-significant genes (FDR<0.05, T2S1) onto gene symbols and builds a high-confidence subnetwork (combined_score>=700)
Reports node degree / hub genes among the interaction gene set relative to the STRING network background

Infers differential transcription-factor activity (e.g., decoupleR ULM/consensus with a human regulon network) for the interaction contrast and for each simple effect, proposing candidate regulators of the genotype-dependent drug response
If either the STRING network or the TF regulon resource is unavailable at run time, explicitly reports that gap and completes whichever of the two analyses is possible rather than failing outright

plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathway/network analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than WT — is a formal statistical interaction question in this 2x2 factorial (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, 4 reps/cell, 16 human brain-tissue RNA-seq samples, 12000 genes). The design supports fitting a single negative-binomial model with a genotype:treatment interaction term rather than four separate pairwise contrasts, so the plan starts with QC/filtering of the raw salmon counts against the 16-sample metadata, then fits DESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, testing the interaction by LRT (the direct answer to the question) alongside the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; within KO) to characterize direction and magnitude of any genotype-dependent difference. Genes flagged by the interaction term are then interpreted at the pathway level (human Hallmark/GO-BP/WikiPathways, matching the Homo sapiens organism of the data) to describe what biology differs, and at the network/regulator level (human STRING PPI plus DoRothEA regulons via decoupleR) to propose which hub genes or transcription factors could drive a genotype-dependent drug response. All reference gene sets used are the human-symbol collections, matching the human counts data.
